title: Seeking truth
subtitle: When you want to know what is real

verses.text: He that trusteth in his own heart is a fool: but whoso walketh wisely, he shall be delivered.
verses.micro: My heart is not a safe guide
verses.insight: I often think I know what's best, but my own understanding can lead me astray.
verses.prayer: Lord, help me to trust Your wisdom over my own.
verses.meaning: In the wisdom tradition of Proverbs, this verse contrasts two paths: the fool who relies on his own flawed and self-deceived inner counsel, and the wise person whose life is guided by God's instruction and thus finds safety.
verses.reflection: My own heart is an unreliable guide, prone to justify my fears and desires; true wisdom comes from humbly seeking the Lord's direction in every step.
verses.fullPrayer: Lord, deliver me from the foolishness of trusting my own understanding; teach me to walk wisely in the light of your truth.

verses.text: Surely the princes of Zoan are fools, the counsel of the wise counsellors of Pharaoh is become brutish: how say ye unto Pharaoh, I am the son of the wise, the son of ancient kings?
verses.insight: Earthly wisdom becomes foolishness apart from God's truth.
verses.prayer: Lord, guard me from trusting my own wisdom.
verses.meaning: The prophet Isaiah declares God's judgment on Egypt's leadership, showing that their celebrated wisdom has become foolish and animal-like, unable to provide Pharaoh with true counsel despite their proud ancestral claims.
verses.reflection: Human wisdom, even when passed down through generations, becomes brutish when disconnected from God's truth, revealing how easily earthly counsel can fail.
verses.fullPrayer: Lord, guard me from trusting in human wisdom that becomes brutish; let my counsel come from you, not from pride in my own heritage or understanding.

verses.text: Confidence in an unfaithful man in time of trouble is like a broken tooth, and a foot out of joint.
verses.insight: I feel helpless when I trust in the wrong things.
verses.prayer: Lord, guard my trust from unfaithful places.
verses.meaning: This proverb warns that relying on someone who proves untrustworthy during a crisis is as painful and disabling as a broken tooth or a dislocated foot, leaving one helpless when help is most needed.
verses.reflection: This verse reveals how spiritual vulnerability comes not just from external trouble, but from misplaced trust that fails when tested, exposing our need for discernment in relationships.
verses.fullPrayer: Lord, guard me from placing my confidence in what is unfaithful, and keep me from becoming like a broken tooth that fails others in their time of trouble.

verses.text: The ancient and honourable, he is the head; and the prophet that teacheth lies, he is the tail.
verses.micro: I am fragile under false leaders
verses.insight: False leaders bring God's judgment on the people.
verses.prayer: Lord, protect me from leaders who deceive.
verses.meaning: In Isaiah's prophecy against Israel's leaders, this verse declares that God will reverse the proper social order as judgment; the respected elders, who should lead, will be humbled, while false prophets, who deceive the people, will be exposed as worthless.
verses.reflection: This verse reveals how spiritual corruption in leadership inverts God's design, turning honor into shame and truth into a lie.
verses.fullPrayer: Lord, guard our hearts from the deception of lies, and establish your truth as the head over all our thoughts and teachings.

verses.text: Am I therefore become your enemy, because I tell you the truth?
verses.micro: I let truth confront my errors.
verses.insight: I recognize that truth can feel like an enemy when it exposes my errors.
verses.prayer: Lord, give me courage to speak and receive truth.
verses.meaning: Paul asks the Galatians if his honest correction of their doctrinal error has turned him into their enemy, highlighting how truth-telling can strain relationships when people prefer comfortable falsehoods.
verses.reflection: Truth often feels like an enemy when it confronts our cherished errors, yet it remains the only path to genuine freedom in Christ.
verses.fullPrayer: Lord, give me courage to speak your truth in love, even when it risks making me an enemy to those who prefer comfortable lies.

verses.text: Butter and honey shall he eat, that he may know to refuse the evil, and choose the good.
verses.micro: I become what I feed my soul
verses.insight: The child's simple diet will shape his moral discernment.
verses.prayer: Lord, nourish me with Your truth so I grow in wisdom.
verses.meaning: In this prophetic sign given to King Ahaz, the child Immanuel will eat the simple, natural foods of the land (curds and honey) as he grows, signifying both a time of agricultural scarcity and his development into moral discernment.
verses.reflection: Just as physical nourishment shapes growth, so our spiritual diet—what we feed our minds and hearts—forms our capacity to distinguish God's good from the world's evil.
verses.fullPrayer: Lord, nourish me with your truth, that I may grow in wisdom and clearly choose the good you desire.

verses.text: Now therefore let Pharaoh look out a man discreet and wise, and set him over the land of Egypt.
verses.micro: I need wisdom for God's warnings
verses.insight: Ignoring divine warnings invites preventable disaster.
verses.prayer: Lord, grant me wisdom to act on Your guidance.
verses.meaning: Joseph, having interpreted Pharaoh's dreams as a warning of coming famine, advises the ruler to appoint a capable administrator to oversee Egypt's preparation and survival. This is practical counsel from a man who recognizes God's revelation requires human wisdom and action to implement.
verses.reflection: Divine warning calls for human stewardship; God's providence often flows through the discernment and diligence of those appointed to lead. Joseph's advice reminds us that spiritual insight must be coupled with practical planning.
verses.fullPrayer: Lord, grant me the discretion and wisdom to recognize Your guidance and to act responsibly when entrusted with care for others. Help me to be a faithful steward over whatever land You place me in.

verses.text: Cast thy bread upon the waters: for thou shalt find it after many days.
verses.micro: I trust God with unseen kindness.
verses.insight: I can give generously without knowing the return, trusting God's timing.
verses.prayer: Lord, help me trust You with my kindness.
verses.meaning: The Teacher (Qoheleth) uses the image of casting bread on water—a seemingly wasteful act—to teach that wise living involves taking faithful, generous actions even when the outcome is uncertain or delayed.
verses.reflection: This verse invites me to trust God with acts of kindness and faithfulness that may seem to disappear like bread sinking in water, knowing He oversees the harvest in His time.
verses.fullPrayer: Lord, help me to cast my bread upon the waters in faith today, trusting that You will bring the fruit of obedience to light after many days.

verses.text: For they are a nation void of counsel, neither is there any understanding in them.
verses.micro: I need God's wisdom to truly see.
verses.insight: A people without God's counsel lacks true understanding.
verses.prayer: Lord, fill me with Your wisdom and understanding.
verses.meaning: In Moses's prophetic song, this verse describes Israel's spiritual condition when they abandon God's ways, portraying them as a people lacking divine wisdom and discernment, which leads to foolish decisions and eventual judgment.
verses.reflection: This verse reveals how spiritual blindness begins when we stop seeking God's counsel, leaving us to navigate life with only our limited understanding.
verses.fullPrayer: Lord, keep me from becoming a person void of Your counsel; fill my heart with Your understanding so I may walk in Your wisdom today.

verses.text: Folly is set in great dignity, and the rich sit in low place.
verses.insight: When I look past the surface, my heart finds truth.
verses.prayer: Lord, help me see beyond the surface.
verses.meaning: The Teacher observes the world's upside-down order, where foolish people are given positions of high honor, while those with true capability or wealth are unjustly placed in low positions.
verses.reflection: This verse exposes how easily human systems confuse appearance with substance, honoring the loud or cunning while overlooking genuine wisdom.
verses.fullPrayer: Lord, when I see folly exalted, keep my heart from cynicism and help me honor what you value, not what the world celebrates.
